{{Quote|We haven't figured out what it is, but we think it may be viral. We haven't announced it yet&mdash;kinda hoping to get everything settled quiet-like&mdash;but we're under quarantine. Nobody's leaving until the agent is isolated.|Nevan Khash, on the virus detected in the ventilation system of the landing bay that he oversaw on Tilnes|<ref name="CA" />}}
'''Nevan Khash''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] individual who worked as a [[Supervisor/Legends|supervisor]] for the [[Verga Mer Mining Company]] corporate concern on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Tilnes]] during the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], while on duty at a [[Hangar/Legends|landing bay]] on Tilnes, Khash identified the presence of a [[Anti-Caarite virus|viral contaminant]] with in the bay's ventilation system and detected a [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]] originating from a purportedly [[Metatheran Cartel Tilnes base|abandoned facility]] between the surface of Tilnes. Terrified by the situation he found himself in, Khash placed the landing bay under quarantine and engaged a team of [[Heroes of Cularin|freelance agents]] to investigate the distress signal and source of the virus.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Maybe you can help. The regular employees are too scared to death to do anything.|Nevan Khash, asking the heroes of Cularin for assistance|<ref name="CA" />}}
Nevan Khash was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] individual employed by the [[Verga Mer Mining Company]] commercial concern on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Tilnes]] in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]] during the latter [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Khash was employed as a [[Supervisor/Legends|supervisor]], in charge of a crew of VMMC personnel who operated a [[Hangar/Legends|landing bay]] within a [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] on Tilnes.<ref name="CA" />

Circa [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]],<ref name="date">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign is set one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As the ''Living Force'' adventure ''[[Below the Belt: Philology|Philology]]'' [[Cularin's disappearance|moved]] the campaign forward ten years to the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the events depicted in ''[[Metatheran Caution: Caaried Away|Caaried Away]]'' can therefore be dated to circa [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]].</ref> while Khash was on duty an [[Electromagnetic pulse/Legends|electromagnetic pulse]] emanated from the core of Tilnes and temporarily shut down all electrical systems at Khash's landing bay. Though the EMP blast initially caused Khash little concern as such blackouts were a common occurrence on Tilnes, beneath the surface of the moon the blast triggered the release of an [[Anti-Caarite virus|experimental virus]] from a [[Metatheran Cartel Tilnes base|base]] of the [[Metatheran Cartel]] trade alliance. The contagion quickly entered the ventilation system of the Khash's landing bay and the supervisor soon detected some unusual [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] readings indicating the presence of the viral contagion. He also detected a [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]] originating from the Cartel facility. The Cartel had publicly claimed to withdrawn from Tilnes<ref name="CA" /> following outcry in the Cularin [[Star system/Legends|system]] about their presence on the moon,<ref name="TR">{{LivingForce|Broken Orbits: Tilnes Rising}}</ref> but Khash had previously heard rumors that the Cartel had secretly remained on Tilnes and paid bribes to the VMMC to conceal the Cartel's operation. He therefore viewed the distress signal as substantive proof that the rumors were true.<ref name="CA" />

Petrified by the spread of the unknown virus and the potential connection of the contagion to the Metatheran Cartel, Khash had his crew hand out [[Breath mask/Legends|respirators]] to everyone present in the landing bay. He also placed the bay under an unofficial state of quarantine, preventing anyone from leaving until the nature of the virus and the origin of the suspicious distress signal could be determined. However, he found that his staff were unwilling to investigate the cause of the occurrences.<ref name="CA" />

{{RPG|''[[Metatheran Caution: Caaried Away|Caaried Away]]''}}
The [[heroes of Cularin]], a group of freelance agents renowned in the Cularin system, were among those passing through Khash's landing bay and made enquiries to him about why the hangar had been locked down. Khash was initially dismissive of their request and instructed the operatives to return to their [[Starship/Legends|starship]], insisting that everything was being handled. Nonetheless, he was familiar with the agents' past exploits and soon recognised them. Seizing the opportunity to resolve his troubled situation, Khash pleaded with the operatives to investigate the viral contaminant and distress signal on his behalf. While he conversed with them he carried a [[Scrambler/Legends|scrambler]] upon his person so as to prevent and recordings from being taken of his entreaty.<ref name="CA" />

The freelancers agreed to assist and Khash provided them with a [[Datachip/Legends|datachip]] that contained the co-ordinates of the distress signal. The agents subsequently identified the source of the distress signal and procured a sample of the virus for analysis. Upon their return to the landing bay, Khash was no longer on duty and nowhere to be found.<ref name="CA" />
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Things'll be straightened soon enough. You just go back to your ship. Everything's under control.|Nevan Khash, while panicking about the virus and distress signal that he had detected|<ref name="CA" />}}
Nevan Khash was a small and slope-shouldered individual. A weak-minded, paranoid and nervous man, he did not cope with stressful situations or being put under pressure, becoming anxious and evasive. He had little skill at bluffing or concealing the truth and so required little coercion to be persuaded to disclose details of his concerns.<ref name="CA" />

Khash did not manage well when faced with the dilemma of how to respond to the distress signal from the Cartel base and the indications of an unidentified virus in the landing bay that he oversaw, becoming distraught and fearing that his life was at risk. He was concerned that he could loose his job if he did not resolve the situation and if he caused alarm by alerting the travelers passing through his landing bay of his findings.<ref name="CA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Nevan Khash featured in ''[[Metatheran Caution: Caaried Away|Caaried Away]]'', a [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure by [[Morrie Mullins (real person)|Morrie Mullins]] that was released in [[March]] [[2003]] and served as the opening instalment of the [[Metatheran Caution trilogy]] of the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|Living Force]] campaign. The adventure does not confirm Khashs' [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="CA" />

In ''Caaried Away'', the players roleplay as the heroes of [[Cularin/Legends|Cularin]]; it is suggested that if the players initially fail to deduce that something unusual is leaking into the landing bay on Tilnes then Khash can take a more proactive role in alerting them to the situation. It is then possible for the players to accept or dismiss Khash's plea for help. If the player do not initially agree to assist him, Khash reluctantly proffers the freelance agents payment of 500 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] out of his personal funds to investigate the mystery. The players can also coerce Khash to disclose his suspicions that the Cartel had never closed down its facility on Tilnes, in which case Khash begs them not to tell anyone that they learned of the Cartel's secret presence on Tilnes from him. After arriving at the Cartel base, it is possible for the player characters to contact Khash to communicate their findings.<ref name="CA" />
